newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks score record closing high.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks score record closing high.

text.p: A sudden, late surge in Hong Kong share prices pushed the Hang Seng index to a record close on Wednesday, as market resilience amid calls for consolidation prompted investors to stick with the rally, analysts said.
A burst of activity in the last hour of trade pushed the Hang Seng index up 143.81 points to a record closing high of 12,250.57, it highest level of the session.
The previous record close set by the blue chip index was 12,201.09 hit on January 4, 1994, The existing record intra-day high was also registered on that day at 12,599.23.
"Investors don't believe the market will have a big correction and they think 12,000 will be a support area," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.
Trading got off to a slow start on Wednesday, with the Hang Seng index ending Wednesday morning's session down 25.02 points at 12,081.74.
Analysts had expected the market to pause after jumping 227.56 points on Monday and slipping 26.31 points on Tuesday.

"In the morning, investors and fund managers were expecting some kind of consolidation following a weak Wall Street," said Tang. "But when the market closed in the morning, it was off only 25 points. Investors started to move back in once the selling pressure was off."

Traders said European funds had prompted the rally in the final hour of trade. By the end of the day turnover had risen to HK$6.21 billion (US$796 million) compared to HK$2.99 billion at the end of the morning session. Turnover was HK$7.14 billion on Tuesday.

"We assume it must be from European buyers. The market was quiet until lunch time, then woke up in the second half when Europe becomes more active," said Miles Remington, sales trader at Crosby Securities.
Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities, said investors began to change their position once they saw that the 12,000 point level on the Hang Seng would be difficult to challenge.

"Yesterday people tried to push the index down but it seems that it cannot break below 12,000, so people are changing their positions. In the futures market, a lot of big investors had short positions this morning and are changing to long positions," he said.
October Hang Seng futures rose 130 points to 12,265.
Property and banking stocks led the charge on Wednesday.
Hang Seng Bank Ltd hit a record intra-day high of HK$87.25 and closed up HK$2.75 at HK$87.00. HSBC Holdings Plc also hit an intra-day record at HK$148.00 and ended up HK$1.50 at HK$147.50.
Henderson Land Development Ltd rose HK$1.50 to HK$69.75, Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd rose HK$1.50 to HK$86.00 and Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd added HK$1.00 to HK$62.00.
"I think people continue to hold a very optimistic view on the Hong Kong property market," said Edward Chan, research director at NAVA SC Securities.

Analysts said with concerns about higher interest rates calmed following the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged at its September meeting, and the prospects of solid earnings growth in 1997, investors continued to hold a bullish view on Hong Kong.

"Right now I don't see any major negatives or market moving factors on the horizon. The interest rate concerns are off and we won't see it probably till after the U.S. election. Local fundamentals are improving and the China factor could becomne more positive," said Tang.
He said the Hang Seng index could reach 13,000 points by the end of the month.

Tang said the record intra-day high of 12,599.23 could present strong resistance, "but with this kind of increased volume and big interest we should not have any problem at all piercing this resistance level".
